Record car sales in October. So why are car stocks down? Ten auto stocks, what they sell, and where.
Maruti Suzuki. Two lakh seventy six thousand cars. Top seller, Wagon R. Exports to a hundred countries. Stock, down twelve percent in a year.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. Tata cars plus Jaguar Land Rover. Top seller, Nexon. J L R sells in the UK, US, China and Europe. Down twenty seven percent.
Mahindra. Record SUV month. Top seller, Scorpio. Big in South Africa and Australia. Down five percent.
Hyundai India. Eighty two thousand cars. Top seller, Creta. Exports to Middle East, Africa, Latin America. Down thirteen percent.
Bajaj Auto. India's biggest bike exporter. Pulsar at home, Boxer from Brazil to Nigeria. Up nineteen percent.
TVS Motor. Seven lakh vehicles. Top seller, Jupiter. Eighty plus countries. Best of the ten, up thirty percent.
Hero MotoCorp. India's number one two wheeler maker. Top seller, Splendor. Colombia to Bangladesh. Down five percent.
Eicher, owner of Royal Enfield. Top seller, Classic three fifty. Strong in Brazil and North America. Up sixteen percent.
Ashok Leyland. Trucks and buses, sales up twenty three percent. Gulf, Africa, South Asia. Stock, down two percent.
Tata Motors trucks. Sales up twenty seven percent, and it now owns most of Italy's Iveco. Up twenty six percent.
The pattern? All four carmakers fell. Bikes and trucks rose. Record sales don't always mean a rising stock.
